title: Weekly inference ops prep: cadence, risk items, action tracker
content:
Quick context (for myself):
- Sync purpose: align serving + infra + console on the next 7 days of work, surface risks to the Dedicated rollout, and lock owners for follow-ups. Keep it tight — 30 min.
- Tone: blunt status + decisions. Save design debates for separate deep-dive.

Agenda (30 min):
1) 5m — Standup-style fast statuses (what blocked last week, what shipping this week).
2) 8m — High-risk items and mitigation proposals. Focus: Dedicated capacity rollout (canary), KV caching regression, routing fallback flakiness.
3) 8m — Console/observability asks: new token-level cost view (spike), per-route latency heatmap missing tail. Decide short-term workaround.
4) 5m — Action-item review + owners + deadlines.
5) 4m — Parking lot & next steps.

Prep notes / talking points:
- Dedicated canary: last canary (region-us-west-2) saw a 9% increase in p95 for cross-shard requests during peak. Most likely cause: autoscaler bump timing + kernel selection mismatch on quantized models.
  - Data: 2026-03-10 peak window 11:05-11:20: p50 32ms, p95 342ms (baseline p95 ~ 310ms).
  - Hypothesis A: autoscaler adds nodes but routing still pushes longer KV cache warmups to new nodes.
  - Hypothesis B: new cuda kernel path (from PR #942) interacts poorly with seq len distribution >1024.
  - Ask: Ethan to summarize quick perf diffs (kernel on/off) and Priya to validate autoscaler logs.

- KV cache regression: some small customers report hallucinated prefixes when hitting fallback model variant. Possible cache key normalization bug introduced in INF-2684.
  - Repro steps needed; ask Diego to pair with customer success to get a repro.

- Routing fallback flakiness: intermittent 504s when fallback kicks in — likely related to circuit-breaker debounce thresholds. Consider temporary increase debounce to 10s for canary region.

Console / Observability:
- Token-level cost view: spike in compute-cost-per-token for long-chat sessions. UX team rolled out the breakdown but backend aggregation is missing summation across streaming chunks. Quick patch: aggregate at router before streaming chunking, then patch metrics processor.
  - Short term: add a 'coarse' cost metric to dashboards to avoid misleading per-chunk spikes.
  - Owner: Priya (backend) + Lina (console) to ship coarse metric by 2026-03-16.

- Latency heatmap: per-route heatmap currently excludes cached prefix hits -> underestimates tail. Manual workaround: export raw request logs to temp dashboard; long term fix is to include cache-hit dimension in ingestion.

Oncall backlog notes:
- OSC-alerts: increase severity for kv-cache-ttl-evictions (recently caused customer-facing errors). SRE to review thresholds.
- I left a note for SRE rotation next week: ensure someone is assigned to the Dedicated canary window (Wed 10:30-12:30 PST).

Decision proposals I want on-call to sign off on during sync:
- Proposal 1: Pause canary expansion until kernel path validated (opt-in fallback).
- Proposal 2: Short-term debounce increase for routing fallback in canary region.
- Proposal 3: Temporary 'coarse' cost metric in console until streaming aggregation fix is deployed.

Action items (short and visible) — keep this lockstep in the sync and update after meeting:
- AI-1: Ethan Cruz — run perf comparison (PR #942 kernel path on vs off) across representative seq-len buckets and upload CSV; due 2026-03-14.
- AI-2: Priya Nair — implement coarse cost metric at router and add to dashboard; due 2026-03-16.
- AI-3: Diego Morales — pair with CS (Nicole) to get a reproducible KV-cache regression example and create a failing test; due 2026-03-15.
- AI-4: SRE (oncall) — bump routing debounce for canary region to 10s during Wed canary window and monitor 5-min error rate; confirm by 2026-03-12 (before canary).
- AI-5: Lenora Hayes (me) — publish a short runbook snippet for canary expansion criteria and share in #serving-ops; due 2026-03-13.
- AI-6: Lina (Console) — add visibility toggle for `include_cache_hits` on the heatmap export; coordinated with Priya; due 2026-03-20.

Open questions / TODOs I want the group to resolve quickly:
- If kernel is the cause, do we gate the PR or add a config toggle? (cost of toggle: testing + complexity).
- Is there a simple observable signal that predicts p95 rises before canary expands (so we can abort earlier)?
- For the KV-cache repro: how many customers are affected? Need quick impact estimate (low/medium/high) to prioritize fix.

Random scribbles I might reference in meeting:
- Linear ticket draft: "canary-kernel-rollback-plan" (work in progress).
- Slack threads: #infra-kernels, #dedicated-rollout (pin relevant messages before meeting).
- Quick measurement: 99th percentile tail correlates with cache-miss ratio > 0.22 in last hour.

Notes after meeting (placeholder to update):
- Decisions taken: (fill after)
- Owners confirm they accept AI-by dates (update list)
- Anything pushed to parking lot: schedule follow-up technical deep-dive (60m) next Tue.

Personal checklist before sending notes to team:
- [ ] Clip the perf graphs (Ethan) and attach to meeting notes.
- [ ] Ping SRE rotation calendar and add canary coverage.
- [ ] Create follow-up calendar invite for kernel deep-dive if required.

Slack post blurb (draft):
"Quick update from today's inference ops sync: we flagged a p95 regression in the us-west canary tied to new kernel behavior. Ethan is running perf diffs; Priya will ship a coarse cost indicator for consoles. We're pausing canary expansion until we validate kernel impact. Full notes + AIs in the doc (linked)."

End of scratchpad. Update this doc after the sync and mark status -> in_review or final as appropriate.
